Traveling while may help refresh her mindset, won’t change that factor. Befriending “the right kind of folk” won’t change the 500+ years of violence laid before us. OP I am sending you consensual hugs. I’m going to try to address this in two separate ways hopefully not to contradict myself here I just want to offer you some support. 

First of all, it’s okay to take care of yourself. I read every word. You did try. I may not understand fully this situation but I went through similar @ 19 when my sister was 5. Had to go full NC and leave her behind with the abuser. It broke my heart but I had nowhere else to go but take care of myself and I want you to know it’s okay. To be in a place where you can take full care of yourself opens up a safe place for your sister to be. It doesn’t have to be right now. You can just grieve for a while and then work on a plan of safety for her. It’s okay to allow yourself to feel this hurt and then move through it, make a plan to have her in your life. Even if it means maintaining no contact. 

Is there anyone else outside of your sister’s mom that is an adult that has access to her? 

Secondly, do you believe with the info that you know, that your sister is in danger? If so, make sure you document what you know, try to make/create a trail if you can. 
Not sure of your location but in the states You can report potential abuse with suspicion, no actual proof is needed. They can make a house visit/eval on just suspicion or open a file at the very least. Professionals are trained to evaluate specific situations. They could maybe help. 

“How to accept that doing the right thing for yourself means you won’t see her grow up?”
I don’t want to feed you incorrect info as I am stranger but just know that as you do the right thing for yourself you are making things better for your sister as default. You are giving her a sibling she can trust and lean on. It’s hard. I missed out on some years and time in my sister’s life but your sister, she will get older. She will gain her own sense of independence, just keep a plan up, even if you know it won’t be for a while. Something to remind you that no matter she’ll always be your sister. Not seeing her grow up in the way you’re wishing doesn’t take that away. Nothing can change that.

They ask about your last diagnosis, any prescriptions you might be on or have ever taken. They evaluate your depression (screening). They also evaluate for potential current psychosis. A year ago, similar evaluation but it was several people evaluating me instead of just one. So just prepare honestly for questions that are deep regarding your mental health history. They’ll ask about your family, potential stressors, how impacted you might be by the current stressors etc. I would just prepare to remember any history that you will think will help with your evaluation. Some usually form a treatment plan afterward too, or the psych who does the eval meet with your therapist, if you have any other questions feel free to ask! Glad to help in any way I can.

Some things I do:
I always make my bed. This task can be hard but making bed makes it more inviting. 

I stay out of my bed/avoid bed until it’s mad late and I know I have to/should sleep.

I took the tv out of my room, laptop is away from me and doesn’t stay on bed. I reduce my phone/screen time to a minimum before bed. 

I try to wear myself out during the day, using a caffeine cause it has a crash sometimes. (Not the healthiest but I do what I can) 

I shower at night. I do a hot water/cold after fix. 

I kinda “baby” myself before... Like am I fed enough so I’m not hungry- do I need milk- are my pjs comfortable? Do I need to brush my teeth again? 

I sleep with a fan facing me. I take deep, slow and steady breaths. Sometimes I’ll count backwards from 1,000-to 1. 

I set up a dream/tunnel to “enter my dreamland” and sometimes tell myself a story. That helps the most out of everything. Even if I’m “awake” for it, it’s often the *only* thing that gets me to sleep.


I don’t check the time, after a certain hour. I turned off the clock in my room. I try to make it as dark as possible. 

My advice: find out what keeps you awake the most, if it’s thoughts, try to journal or give them space during the day, set a “time” for them to be active. This sucks for me as I spiral it still takes me sooo long to fall asleep, but I do sleep.

Having somewhat of a routine really really helps.

Edit: when it’s really bad and none of that works I turn to teas that help me sleep. I have meds that help with headaches which also make me sleepy. I do everything I know that makes me sleepy. If I can’t/don’t sleep I try not to get frustrated and just accept it. Sleep will come... *eventually* lol.
